Order 
The accused in C.C.No.3087 of 2001 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Pattambi, filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 r/w Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Pattambi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 12.11.2001 at about 12 p.m., PW2, the Food Inspector purchased three packets of tamarind, each packet contained 500 gram each, from the accused.
It is alleged that the revision petitioner sold the food time without having a valid PFA licence.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts.P1 to P11 were marked for the prosecution.
No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.

5. The courts below correctly evaluated the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution and concurrently found that the revision petitioner did not possess any valid licence under the PFA Rules to sell the food item.

No circumstance has been brought to the notice of this court by the learned counsel for the revision petitioner to indicate that the concurrent finding of conviction by the courts below is perverse or incorrect.

In the said circumstances, the concurrent finding by the courts below that the revision petitioner committed the offence under Sections 16 (1)
(a) (ii) and 7 (iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 r/w Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 does not warrant any interference by this court.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 r/w
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. As regards the sentence, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has pleaded for leniency.
The offence was committed during the year 2001.
There is no previous conviction against the revision petitioner.
There was also no allegation that the food item sold by the revision petitioner was adulterated or misbranded.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the sentence in this case can be awarded as provided under the second proviso to Section 16 (1) of the PFA Act and K.I.Ibrahim vs The Food Inspector on 8 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128246312/
2

entities.text: K.I.Ibrahim vs The Food Inspector on 8 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
accordingly, the sentence awarded by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules stands modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/-
(Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for ten days, to meet the ends of Justice.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed in part as above.
The revision petitioner shall surrender before the court below on 1.4.2016 to suffer the sentence.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl.
